scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Subset Sum in Time $`O(2^{0.49n})`$” (preprints/Subset-Sum-in-Time-2-power-0-49n-October-4-2026/subset-sum.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 138 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 69f9398e325a2628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a uniform randomized classical algorithm A for Subset Sum with the following properties in the word-RAM model (1.1). For every input with n ≥ 2, the algorithm halts on every execution and outputs the correct answer with probability at least 2/3. For every fixed positive integer c, there are constants Cc > 0 and Nc ≥ 2 such that every input with n ≥ Nc and b ≤ nc is processed, on every outcome of the random choices, in at most Cc 20.49n word operations. The program is not given c and does not depend on c.
